description: Replay bounded insert, delete, and membership operations against a deterministic extendible hash directory.

source.title: Extendible Hashing – A Fast Access Method for Dynamic Files
source.authors: R. Fagin, J. Nievergelt, N. Pippenger, and H. R. Strong
source.reference: ACM Transactions on Database Systems 4(3), pages 315-344 (1979)
source.pinned_behavior: Low-order key bits index a directory. A full bucket splits at its local-depth boundary and doubles the directory only when local depth equals global depth. Deletion applies deterministic buddy coalescing and directory shrinking.

input.hash_function: h(key)=key; directory uses the lowest global_depth bits

output.encoding: bits 0..39 contain operation-success bits in trace order (oldest at the most-significant used bit); bits 40..48 are final active bucket count; bits 49..52 final global depth; bits 53..56 maximum global depth reached; bits 57..62 final live-key count
output.success_rule: Insert succeeds only for an absent key; delete succeeds only for a present key; membership succeeds only when the key is present.

contract.directory_growth: When an overflowing bucket has local_depth equal to global_depth, duplicate the current directory into its upper half and increment global_depth. Split the bucket by the next key bit and redirect matching directory aliases.
contract.bucket_identity: Native bucket storage reuses the lowest inactive identifier; identifiers do not appear in output.
contract.deletion: After removal, repeatedly merge with the same-depth buddy if the combined contents fit in one capacity-2 bucket. The bucket with the lower suffix prefix survives. Shrink while the two directory halves are identical, but never below depth 1.
contract.max_depth: Maximum global depth reached during the trace; deletion never reduces this high-water field.
contract.initial_state: Two empty buckets with local depth 1 and global depth 1.
contract.complexity: At most 40 operations and 8 split/merge levels. Each directory pass scans at most 256 entries; each split redistributes at most two keys. O(Q*8*256) bounded time (O(Q*256) with fixed depth cap) and O(256) state.

workspace.accounting: Fixed 256-entry directory, 256 bucket records with two byte keys each, local-depth/count/active arrays, and bounded parser/scalar temporaries; caller input is excluded.
